the role of calcium (Ca2+) in the regulation of orexin receptor function and orexin receptor‐coupled signal transduction pathways in the central nervous system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
orexin A is a potent orexin receptor agonist that is able to activate both OX1R and OX2R, with a preference for OX2R.
orexin‐A stimulation of OX1 receptors induces Ca2+ influx via ROCs and SOC, and that these pathways can be differentially regulated by the intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
OX1 receptor‐mediated PLC activation is regulated by both ROCs and SOCs, but that SOCs are the dominant pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OX1‐PLC pathway is regulated by Ca2+ in a manner that is dependent on the Ca2+ influx pathway activated.
OX1 receptor‐mediated PLC activation is dependent on the presence of Ca2+, which is required to activate both the ROCs and the SOC.
OX1‐induced Ca2+ elevating pathways do indeed amplify PLC signalling in HEK‐293 and CHO‐K1 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OX1 receptor‐coupling efficiency to PLC is enhanced by Ca2+‐dependent positive feedback mechanisms, which are mediated by SOC channels.
Ca2+‐induced Ca2+ release (CICR) is a key mechanism that couples orexin‐A stimulation to PLC activation.
the Ca2+‐sensitive amplification of orexin‐mediated PLC signalling occurs primarily via the SOC pathway.
